subject: Post-discovery: scheduling ML runbook session and constraints
messages:
From: Samantha Ruiz <samantha@medstream.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: ops@medstream.com
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from discovery — request to schedule a 60-90m ML runbook session

Hi Kimberly & Ben,

Thanks again for the call earlier — that was really helpful. Our team is keen to follow up with a deeper session that includes our ML/platform engineers and your infra folks so we can:
- Walk through integration points (auth, ingress, data flow)
- Validate latency/cost expectations for our traffic profile
- Align on runbook, fallbacks, and monitoring thresholds

We'd like a 60–90 minute technical runbook session with your ML/infra engineers. Proposed windows (Pacific):
- Thu Aug 5, 10:00–11:30 PT
- Fri Aug 6, 09:00–10:30 PT
- Wed Aug 11, 11:00–12:30 PT

Attendees on our side: Samantha Ruiz (Director, ML Eng), Tom Lee (Platform Eng).
Can you confirm who from Redwood should be in the room and share a draft agenda / pre-reads? Also let us know if you need QPS / token distribution data in advance.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Ruiz
Director of ML Engineering
MedStream, Inc.

--
Attachment: medstream-discovery-notes.txt (text)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Samantha Ruiz <samantha@medstream.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from discovery — request to schedule a 60-90m ML runbook session

Thanks Samantha — great to hear the team is ready to move into the technical runbook.

We can staff the session with:
- Kimberly Park (Account Exec) — covers timeline/rollout coordination
- Ben Carter (Solutions Engineer) — will lead the deep technical runthrough
- Neha Kapoor (Platform SWE) — will handle infra, autoscaling, and security questions

I've attached a quick draft agenda (ML_runbook_agenda_v1.pdf). High level we propose:
1) 5m intros and outcomes
2) 20–30m architecture & integration review
3) 20–30m performance expectations (latency, batching, caching)
4) 15m runbook & fallback patterns (canary, model variant fallback)
5) 10–15m next steps & action items

From the slots you suggested, Fri Aug 6 at 09:00 PT looks promising for our engineers. Can you confirm timezone for each attendee and share QPS / token distribution if available? Also: do you want a short SOC2 overview in the session (we can cover access controls + logging) or should we keep that to a separate compliance call?

If Aug 6 works, we'll send a calendar invite + Zoom and include the draft agenda.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from discovery — request to schedule a 60-90m ML runbook session

Kimberly — I'll lead the technical sections. A few items I want to put on the agenda to make the session actionable:
- Short run of MedStream's expected traffic profile (QPS, tokens per request, burst patterns) — if you can share a CSV we can synthesize a load profile ahead of time
- KV caching / prefix caching patterns and where to place caching (app vs runtime)
- Expected latency SLOs and how batching affects p50/p95 under target batch sizes
- Model variants & quantization tradeoffs for cost/latency
- Fallback routing (region/capacity) and a simple runbook playbook for incidents

If Aug 6 @ 09:00 PT is the chosen slot, please confirm attendee emails and whether you want a short (5–10m) SOC2-controls overview during the call. I'll bring a short deck and we can run the architecture and an ops checklist in parallel.

I'll also drop a short precall questionnaire (precall-questionnaire.docx) in the shared Drive to collect QPS/token numbers and current infra constraints.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
